name: AI
summary: Products from photos, listing rewrites, review and ads summaries, a capped AI gateway, read-only agent keys and MCP, and what is not built.
title: AI in GoCommerce — Gateway, Agent Keys and MCP
description: GoCommerce’s AI, checked against the code: products from photos, listing rewrites and review summaries, on a gateway that caps and records every call.
ogTitle: AI in GoCommerce, feature by feature
ogDescription: Products drafted from photos, better listings and review summaries on a capped, recorded AI gateway. Read-only agent keys, MCP, and what is not built yet.
h1: Model calls on a budget, agents on read-only keys
lede: GoCommerce calls a model in one place, the AI gateway, which records every call, holds each store to its AI credit or to its own key and cap, and sends only the data its owner lets out. Four tools in the panel run through it: products drafted from a batch of photos, a better listing for a product already in the catalogue, a summary of a product’s reviews, and a summary of the ads report. An AI agent gets a key of its own that only reads, and reaches the store through the MCP server. A store hosted on admin.kitcommerce.store has the gateway and the four tools on the platform’s own Claude key, with a free trial of AI credit; MCP is a module you install when you run GoCommerce yourself.

facts.t: kinds of store data, each a switch the owner sets
MCP tools, the {mcpReadTools} that read offered to an agent key

groups.name: AI tools in the panel
groups.lede: Buttons a person presses on the store’s own products and reviews. Each is a task on the AI gateway below, so it is recorded, paid from the store’s AI credit or held to its own cap, and sent only the data the owner lets out.

tiles.title: Products from a batch of photos
tiles.text: Create from photos, on the products screen, takes up to 60 photos at a time. The AI sorts them into products, with the angles of one item as its pictures and its other colours or finishes as variants, and writes each product’s title, description, highlights, type, tags, category, SEO copy and alt text from what the photos show. The shop renames, moves a photo, merges, splits or leaves one out, then presses Create.

tiles.title: Created as drafts with no price
tiles.text: Each product is created as a draft, every variant at price 0 with nothing in stock, so no shopper can buy it and the products list’s Needs a price filter finds it. Sizes come only from the shop, as a Size option, and a suggested new category is never created. A batch that stops picks up where it left off and never makes a product twice.

tiles.title: A better listing for a product you sell
tiles.text: Improve with AI on a product’s page proposes a new title, description, highlights, tags, type, category, SEO copy and alt text, each beside the current value with a reason. A list names what the model inferred, such as a material or a fit, for the shop to check. Apply selected copies the ticked fields into the form. Nothing is written until the shop saves.

tiles.title: No prices or ratings in AI copy
tiles.text: Create from photos and Improve with AI are told to write only what the shop’s own words or the photos show: never a price, discount, stock level, rating, review or “bestseller”, and no material, size or origin that cannot be seen. Improve with AI also drops any proposed line that names a price, discount, stock level, rating, review or bestseller. It is never sent a product’s prices, stock or orders.

tiles.title: What shoppers praise and complain about
tiles.text: Summarize reviews, on the Reviews screen, sorts a product’s published reviews into themes under fit, quality, colour, delivery, value and other, each listing the reviews that say it, beside the average rating. The average and the counts are worked out in code from the reviews each theme cites, not by the model. Below three reviews no model is asked, an unchanged set is answered from the cache for 30 days, and no shopper’s name or email is sent.

tiles.title: Ads report in plain words
tiles.text: The ads report shows orders, sales, refunds and profit after product cost by source, medium and campaign, against spend typed in or imported from Google Ads and Meta Ads Manager. Summarize writes it up in plain words from the report’s own rows, and an answer that states a number not in them is refused. A weekly summary is off until the shop turns it on.

groups.name: The AI gateway
groups.lede: ext/ai-gateway, installed with -ai-gateway or in your own main(), and brought in by -photo-products, -catalog-ai and -ads. With an Anthropic key for the install in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, every store has AI with nothing to set up. Without one, it stays idle until a store gives it a key, a monthly cap and a price for each model.

tiles.title: The install’s key, or the store’s own
tiles.text: A store that enters no key runs on the install’s Anthropic key, at the models and prices the install sets, with the gateway on and pictures allowed from the start. A store may paste its own Anthropic or OpenAI key instead, and is then billed by its provider and draws no credit. Check connection lists the models a store’s own key reaches without spending tokens.

tiles.title: Pay-per-use AI credit
tiles.text: A call on the install’s key is paid from the store’s AI credit: a free trial allowance each store starts with, plus what the install’s operator tops up with the admin token. The most a call could cost is held before it goes out and settled to the real cost after, so a failed call or a cached answer costs nothing. A store with no credit left is refused before any model is called. The AI screen shows the free trial left, the topped-up balance and what is spent.

tiles.title: A monthly cap that holds
tiles.text: A cap in the store’s currency per calendar month, needed with the store’s own key and optional on the install’s, where the credit is the limit. Before each call its worst-case cost is reserved in one conditional update, so calls running at once cannot spend past it; afterwards it is settled to what the provider reported.

tiles.title: Every run on the record
tiles.text: One row per run: the task, the model, tokens, time taken, the outcome, and the cost as an integer in millionths of a minor unit. The Usage screen adds them up by day, task or model against the cap.

tiles.title: Switches for what leaves the store
tiles.text: Catalogue, order lines, contact details, message bodies and documents. Contact details and message bodies stay in until the owner turns them on, and documents too unless the install runs AI on its own key. Data in a class that is off is dropped before sending, and an email address or international phone number found elsewhere is replaced.

tiles.title: The small model first
tiles.text: Each task names its models in order: the small one first and the strong one only when an answer fails its schema or its own check, with the reason written down. Reading photos goes straight to the strong one. The defaults are Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5. Answers may be reused within one store, never across stores.

tiles.title: A queue for model work
tiles.text: Work is queued in the transaction that caused it and retried only for timeouts, rate limits and outages; the Jobs screen retries or cancels the rest. Missing: a module that queues work. Every task today, from photos to review summaries, runs directly.

groups.name: The approval queue
groups.lede: Where something an agent proposes waits for a person. It is part of the AI gateway.

tiles.title: A person decides
tiles.text: A proposal waits seven days for a person signed in to the panel, holding ai.approve and the action’s own right; an API key or the admin token cannot decide. Approving runs the action as that person. Missing: actions — no module registers one yet, so nothing can be proposed.

tiles.title: It runs what was reviewed
tiles.text: The preview is worked out again when a proposal is opened and again on approval. If the store changed in between, nothing runs and the new preview is shown; two approvals at once run it once.

tiles.title: Every decision on the record
tiles.text: A proposal keeps who filed it, the trace id of the request that did, who approved or rejected it and when, and what the action returned or why it failed.

groups.name: Agent keys
groups.lede: A kind of API key made for an AI agent, on Settings › API keys. Integration keys work as before.

tiles.title: Reads only
tiles.text: An agent key carries a list of rights chosen from its maker’s own instead of a role, and in this release only reads. Some it can never hold: API keys, the team, roles, plugins, store settings, exports, custom SQL reports and webhooks.

tiles.title: Shown once, then it expires
tiles.text: Only its hash is kept, so it is shown once and cannot be copied again. It expires after 90 days unless its maker chooses otherwise, a year at most.

tiles.title: Rate limited
tiles.text: 60 requests a minute unless its maker chooses between 1 and 600, counted in PostgreSQL so the limit holds across servers. Over it, the answer is 429 with Retry-After.

tiles.title: Never more than its maker
tiles.text: On every request the key is cut to what the person who made it holds in the store today. Demote them and the key loses the same rights; remove them and it stops working.

tiles.title: Emails and phones masked
tiles.text: An agent sees customers’ emails and phone numbers masked, and none of the merchant’s notes; it cannot look a customer up by email. The notification log, shipping labels and invoice documents are closed to it, and no right unmasks it.

tiles.title: The audit trail names it
tiles.text: A change made with an API key is recorded as that key, by id and name, and one made with an agent key as the agent, with the run it was doing — not as an unnamed operator.

tiles.title: Store tools for agents
tiles.text: {mcpTools} tools over the same domain services as the REST API, each checked against the caller’s rights, with every change written to an audit table. Over HTTP or stdio.

tiles.title: A read-only mode
tiles.text: Config.ReadOnly withholds all {mcpWriteTools} tools that change things from every caller, the admin token included, and tools/list marks each tool with readOnlyHint.

tiles.title: Agent keys get the read tools
tiles.text: An agent key is offered the read tools only. A tool that changes the store, a module’s own included, is left out of its list and refused and audited if called.

notYetLede: GoCommerce’s AI-Native B2B specification, in the repository under docs/ai-b2b, describes more than the code does. None of the following is built.

notYet.name: Agents that change things
notYet.why: An agent key only reads, and no module registers an action in the approval queue, so an agent cannot propose a change.

notYet.name: Improving many products at once
notYet.why: Improve with AI works on one product at a time; nothing rewrites a whole catalogue in one go.

notYet.name: Buying AI credit
notYet.why: A store cannot pay for credit itself. The install’s operator tops it up with the admin token; on admin.kitcommerce.store, ask us and we add more.

notYet.name: A WhatsApp sales inbox
notYet.why: No WhatsApp connection, shared inbox or suggested replies.

notYet.name: An order desk
notYet.why: Nothing reads a message, an email or a PDF purchase order and drafts an order or a quote from it.

notYet.name: Semantic search
notYet.why: No embeddings are made or stored; search is the engine’s own or Meilisearch’s.

notYet.name: Agent memory
notYet.why: Nothing keeps an agent’s notes or a customer’s preferences between runs.

notYet.name: Procurement and catalogue tools
notYet.why: No supplier catalogue mapping, quote requests to suppliers or product substitution.

notYet.name: Other model providers
notYet.why: Anthropic and OpenAI only, at their own addresses, and the install’s own key is Anthropic’s; no self-hosted or custom endpoint.

faq.q: Does a store need its own AI key?
faq.a: Not on an install that has an Anthropic key of its own in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: every store with no key runs on it, paid from its AI credit. A store may enter its own Anthropic or OpenAI key instead and is billed by that provider. Without an install key, a store needs its own key, a monthly cap and a price for each model before the gateway makes a call.

faq.q: What does the AI cost a store?
faq.a: On the install’s key it is pay-per-use, paid from the store’s AI credit, and each store starts with a free trial allowance. Only a model call draws credit: a cached answer, an answer worked out without a model and every feature that is not AI draw none. A store on its own key pays its provider and draws no credit.

faq.q: Can an AI agent change my store?
faq.a: Not with an agent key: it only reads. An agent handed a person’s credential or the admin token can use MCP’s {mcpWriteTools} tools that change things, each checked against that credential’s rights and audited. The approval queue, which would let an agent propose a change for a person to approve, has no actions yet.

faq.q: What customer data does a model see?
faq.a: Only what the store’s owner allows. The catalogue and order lines may leave by default, and documents too when the install runs AI on its own key; contact details and message bodies stay in until switched on. Review summaries need message bodies on and never send a shopper’s name or email. An agent key sees emails and phone numbers masked whatever the switches say.

faq.q: What uses the AI gateway today?
faq.a: Create from photos and Improve with AI on the products screens, Summarize reviews on the Reviews screen, the ads report’s summary, and the Amazon importer’s rewrite of a listing’s copy. Nothing else in the repository calls a model.

faq.q: How do I run the AI tools?
faq.a: On a store hosted on admin.kitcommerce.store they are already on, with no key to set up, and every new store gets a free trial of AI credit. Or run GoCommerce yourself and start it with -photo-products, -catalog-ai and -ads, which bring -ai-gateway with them, and -reviews for review summaries. Give the engine an Anthropic key in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and every store runs on it; without one, each store sets its own key, cap and prices. For MCP, install ext/mcp in your own main().
